daily_meal_frequency: On demand, day and night (at least 8 to 12 times in 24 hours)
household_portion: On demand breast milk volume; no solid food
preparation_instructions: Feed exclusively on breast milk on demand, day and night.
Ensure proper positioning and latching.
No water, glucose water, formula milk, tea, or animal milk should be given unless ordered by a physician.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Strict ban on solid food and non-breast milk liquids before 6 completed months.
Formula milk should not be encouraged; introduction decided only by a doctor (Booklet inside cover).
Do not feed while distracted by television, mobile phones, or walking around.

household_portion: 2 to 3 teaspoons (can give more if the baby eats)
preparation_instructions: Boil white or red rice soft until grains burst.
Mash thoroughly with a clean spoon to a smooth semi-solid form.
Moisten with expressed breast milk for familiar taste.
Offer 2–3 teaspoons when baby is alert, calm, and slightly hungry.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Strict prohibition: Absolutely no added salt or sugar.
Commercially prepared ultra-processed baby foods and drinks are strictly not recommended.
Wash hands thoroughly with soap before food preparation and feeding.
Feed in a calm designated place; no television or phone screens.

source_citation.evidence_description: Day 1 inception: 2–3 teaspoons of soft mashed rice with expressed breast milk, once a day.

household_portion: Gradually increase the amount at each meal from 2–3 tsp baseline
preparation_instructions: Boil rice soft and mash with a clean spoon.
Gradually increase the amount at each meal based on baby's interest and swallowing comfort.
Continue breastfeeding on demand before and after meals.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: No added salt or sugar.
Use separate, dedicated clean plate and spoon for the baby.
Do not force-feed if the baby turns their head away.

source_citation.evidence_description: Days 2 to 3: soft mashed rice, 1 to 2 meals a day, gradually increasing amount at each meal.

household_portion: 3 to 4 teaspoons or more at a time + 1 teaspoon or more fruit
preparation_instructions: Cook red lentils (dhal) until soft and creamy; mash into puree.
Mash soft boiled rice and combine with dhal puree.
Mash 1 teaspoon of ripe banana or ripe papaya smoothly.
Offer fruit immediately after the meal to enhance iron absorption from dhal.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Single-food introduction rule: Introduce only ONE new food for 2–3 continuous days before introducing another.
No added salt or sugar.
Wash hands and utensils clean.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Days 4 to 6: mashed rice with dhal puree (3–4 tsp or more, twice a day) + 1 tsp or more fruit.

stage_name: Animal Protein & Sprat Powder Inception (Days 7 to 9)
household_portion: Main meal portion building towards 5–6 tsp + ~1 tsp sprat powder + 1–2 tsp fruit
preparation_instructions: Follow FHB Sprat Protocol: Wash whole dried sprats without removing heads, roast/dry, grind whole into fine powder.
Add about 1 teaspoon of sprat powder when preparing meal.
Cook with thick coconut milk or temper with a little bit of pure oil or butter for energy enrichment.
Gradually increase particle size day by day.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Ensure sprat powder is finely ground to eliminate any sharp bone pieces.
If using fresh fish, inspect meticulously and remove all bones.
No added salt or sugar.

source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Days 7 to 9: animal food introduction, FHB sprat protocol (~1 tsp whole sprat powder), coconut milk enrichment.

household_portion: 5 to 6 teaspoons at a time, twice a day + 1 to 2 teaspoons fruit
preparation_instructions: Prepare the 4-part mash combining: (1) Staple rice, (2) Pulse (dhal, green gram, cowpea), (3) Animal food (sprats, fish, chicken, liver), and (4) Yellow vegetable (pumpkin, carrot, yellow sweet potato).
Cook with thick coconut milk or temper with a small dab of butter/oil.
Mash together smoothly into a soft paste.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: No added salt or sugar.
Cook liver and meat thoroughly before finely mincing.
Offer 1–2 teaspoons fruit after meal.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Days 10 to 15: 4-part mash, 5–6 teaspoons twice a day + 1–2 teaspoons fruit.

stage_name: Half-Mashed Rice, Green Leaves & Egg Yolk (Days 16 to 30)
household_portion: About 1/4 of a tea cup at a time + 1 to 2 teaspoons fruit
preparation_instructions: Cook rice to a half-mashed texture (soft tender grains).
Introduce green leafy vegetables (gotukola, murunga leaves, sarana, thampala, mukunuwenna).
FHB Egg Protocol: After 1.5 to 2 weeks of solids, hard-boil an egg, separate yolk, and feed a little bit of boiled egg yolk first.
Cook with thick coconut milk or add a dab of butter/margarine.
Water Protocol: Offer sips of boiled, cooled water after meals.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Egg yolk only; egg white is introduced ~1 week later.
No added salt or sugar.
Offer boiled cooled water in a cup, not a feeding bottle.

source_citation.evidence_description: Days 16 to 30: half-mashed rice (~1/4 tea cup, 2–3 times/day), green leaves, egg yolk, and boiled water sips.

stage_name: 6-Month Introductory Complementary Feeding (General / Start Date Unknown)
daily_meal_frequency: 1 to 3 meals per day progressing gradually
household_portion: Starting from 2–3 tsp progressing towards ~1/4 tea cup + 1–2 tsp fruit
preparation_instructions: Provides age-normative introductory guidance when exact start date is unrecorded:
Begin with soft mashed rice mixed with breast milk.
Follow single-food trial rule (one new food for 2–3 days).
Progress through dhal, whole sprat powder, pumpkin/carrot, green leaves, and boiled egg yolk.
Enrich with thick coconut milk or vegetable oil/butter.
Offer sips of boiled cooled water after meals.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Strict ban on added salt and sugar before 1 year.
No commercial ultra-processed foods.
Wash hands and utensils.

household_portion: 1/2 tea cup at a time + 2 to 3 teaspoons fruit
preparation_instructions: Texture: Coarsely mashed rice, pulses, and vegetables.
Portion: 1/2 tea cup at a time, 2 to 3 times a day + 2 to 3 teaspoons of scraped fruit.
Continue progressive single-food trials and breastfeed after meals.
No between-meal snacks are introduced during this baseline week.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: No added salt or sugar.
Ensure food hygiene: clean hands, cup, plate, and spoon.
Feed patiently in a quiet place without screen distractions.

source_citation.evidence_description: 7 completed months baseline: coarsely mashed, 1/2 tea cup 2–3 times a day + 2–3 tsp fruit, breastfeed after meals.

stage_name: 7 Months + 1 Week (Snack Inception & Whole Egg Trial)
household_portion: 1/2 tea cup at a time + ~4 teaspoons fruit + 1 to 2 snacks
preparation_instructions: Texture: Coarsely mashed.
First introduction of nutritious snacks: offer 1 to 2 snacks between meals (e.g. boiled sweet potato, scraped fruit).
Portion: 1/2 tea cup main meal + ~4 teaspoons fruit + 1 to 2 snacks daily.
Whole Egg Trial: If boiled egg yolk was introduced earlier and tolerated well, trial a little bit of hard-boiled whole egg.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Verify that egg yolk was tolerated before introducing whole egg.
Do not add salt or sugar to snacks or meals.
Offer boiled cooled water after meals and snacks.

source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: 7 months + 1 week: 1/2 tea cup + ~4 tsp fruit + 1–2 snacks per day, whole egg trial if yolk tolerated.

household_portion: 1/2 tea cup at a time + 4 to 5 teaspoons fruit + 1 to 2 snacks
preparation_instructions: Texture: Transition from coarsely mashed towards coarsely chopped vegetables and soft tender foods.
Portion: 1/2 tea cup main meal + 4 to 5 teaspoons fruit + 1 to 2 nutritious snacks daily.
Continue diverse animal-source foods, pulses, and green leaves daily.
Breastfeed on demand after meals.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Ensure vegetable pieces are soft and finely chopped to avoid choking risk.
No added salt or sugar.
Never leave infant unattended while eating.

stage_name: 8 Completed Calendar Months (Traditional Staples & Finger Foods)
household_portion: A bit more than 1/2 tea cup at each meal + ~1/4 tea cup fruit
preparation_instructions: Texture: Coarsely chopped.
Introduce traditional Sri Lankan staples: boiled jak (kos), breadfruit (del), sweet potato, string hoppers.
Introduce supervised finger foods: soft center of hopper, ripe avocado piece, hard-boiled egg wedge, boiled sweet potato wedge.
Portion: A bit more than 1/2 tea cup at each meal + ~1/4 tea cup scraped fruit.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Mandatory Choking Safety: Adult supervision required; child must never be left unattended with finger foods.
No added salt or sugar.
Encourage self-feeding while caregiver assists.

stage_name: 9 to 11 Completed Calendar Months (Separate Curries & Family Table Integration)
household_portion: 3/4 tea cup of food at a time (a bit more at 9m) + ~1/4 tea cup fruit
preparation_instructions: Texture: Coarsely chopped; coarsely mashed at feeding time.
FHB Separate Plate Presentation: Serve rice and curries separately on the plate and mix while feeding.
Seat baby with family members at meal times.
Portion: A bit more than 3/4 tea cup at 9m; 3/4 tea cup at 9–11m.
Offer fruit (~1/4 cup) and finger foods as snacks.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: No added salt or sugar until 1 year of age.
Whole nuts and hard seeds must be crushed/mashed; whole nuts prohibited.
Ensure food hygiene: separate cup, plate, spoon.

source_citation.evidence_description: 9 to 11 months: 3–4 meals + 1–2 snacks, 3/4 tea cup, rice and curries served separately.

stage_name: 12 to 23 Completed Calendar Months (1 to 2 Years)
household_portion: A bit more than 1 tea cup per main meal + full FHB daily requirements table
preparation_instructions: Texture: Wholesome chopped family foods.
Follow FHB 1–2 Years Daily Requirements Table:
- Cereals/staples: 1 1/2 to 2 tea cups daily.
- Cooked pulses: 3 to 6 tablespoons daily.
- Vegetables: 6 tablespoons daily (2 different vegetables).
- Green leaves: 3 tablespoons daily.
- Sprats: 10 to 20 numbers daily OR fish/meat/liver: 2 to 4 matchbox-sized pieces.
- Kunisso: 2 tablespoons daily.
- Eggs: 1 whole egg daily.
- Fruits: twice a day.
- Breastfeed 2 to 3 times a day after meals.
- Non-breastfed dairy substitutes: 1 cup curd OR 1 cup yoghurt OR 1 matchbox-sized cheese.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Mild seasoning only; limit salt and sugar.
Choking hazard rule: Never give whole peanuts or cashews; must be finely crushed/ground.
Manioc must be boiled thoroughly with lid open and water discarded.

stage_name: 24 to 59 Completed Calendar Months (2 to 5 Years)
household_portion: Scaling from > 1 tea cup towards close to 2 tea cups by 5 years + full daily table
preparation_instructions: Wholesome family diet with gradual portion scaling towards close to 2 tea cups.
Follow FHB 2–5 Years Daily Requirements Table:
- Cereals/staples: 2 tea cups or more daily.
- Cooked pulses: 3 to 6 tablespoons daily.
- Vegetables: 6 tablespoons daily (2 different vegetables).
- Green leaves: 3 tablespoons daily.
- Sprats: 20 numbers daily OR fish/meat/liver: 4 matchbox-sized pieces.
- Kunisso: 2 tablespoons daily.
- Eggs: 1 whole egg daily.
- Fruits: twice a day.
- Non-breastfed dairy substitutes: 1 to 2 cups curd/yoghurt or 1 to 2 matchbox pieces cheese.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Avoid ultra-processed commercial snacks, instant noodles, and sugary drinks.
Crush whole nuts before feeding to prevent choking.
Ensure proper handwashing before meals.

stage_name: Completion Boundary (60 Completed Calendar Months / 5th Birthday)
daily_meal_frequency: Family meals as per school-age guidelines
household_portion: Completion notice: Child has completed the 0–59 completed months research component boundary
preparation_instructions: The child has reached their fifth birthday (60 completed calendar months) and completed the target age window of this research component.
No newly generated daily or weekly complementary/preschool nutrition plan is generated.
Direct the caregiver to Family Health Bureau school-age nutrition guidelines and continued family meal variety.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: Continue healthy family eating patterns: plenty of vegetables, green leaves, fruits, and animal-source proteins.
Limit sugar, salt, and ultra-processed foods.

source_citation.publication: Baby Growth Monitoring System Research Scope Specification
source_citation.evidence_description: Agreed project research boundary (0–59 completed months). At 60 completed months, system transitions caregiver to school-age guidance.

stage_name: Late-Starting Complementary Feeding Transition Guidance (Age >= 7m, Start Date <= 30 Days)
daily_meal_frequency: 1 to 2 meals per day initially, building to 2 to 3 meals
household_portion: Introductory progression (2–3 tsp building to ~1/4 cup), adapting to appetite
preparation_instructions: Application-derived transition guidance (Tier B) for late starters:
When complementary feeding begins after 6 completed months, chronological age and complementary feeding start date remain distinct.
Initiate solids with single-food trials (rice, dhal, sprat powder, egg yolk) over the initial weeks to observe digestive tolerance and food acceptance.
Do not automatically apply an entire inflexible 6-month feeding schedule to an older child.
Allow portion amounts and texture progression to scale up more rapidly if the child shows vigorous appetite and tolerates the food well.
safety_and_hygiene_guidance: No added salt or sugar before 1 year.
Monitor tolerance of newly introduced foods carefully.
Ensure adult supervision.
